subject: Mutual action plan: POC scope, model selection & localization checklist
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Mutual action plan: POC scope, model selection & localization checklist

Hi David / Sara —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed mutual action plan so we keep momentum:

Summary of ask:
- Customer goal: Automate triage and first-pass response for patient messaging across English + Spanish + Portuguese; preserve clinical safety and turn-around SLAs.
- Target throughput: ~120 requests/minute peak for triage use case, burst to 200 for campaign windows.

Proposed POC scope (30 days):
1) Integration: Redwood hosted endpoint + test dataset (anonymized), sample traffic replay.
2) Evaluation: Acceptance gates around intent accuracy (macro intent F1 >= 0.88), hallucination checks (manual sample <= 2%), response latency p50 < 250ms, cost estimate per 1k requests.
3) Localization: Spanish + Portuguese prompt templates + evaluation sets (50 examples per locale).
4) Failover: Verify a small on-prem fallback model for air-gapped escalation.

Draft timeline:
- Week 0: Sign MPA and ingest test set (you)
- Week 1: Model selection & baseline runs (us)
- Week 2: Integration + routing config + KV caching setup (joint)
- Week 3: Eval run & acceptance review (joint)
- Week 4: Final decision & handoff to ops (joint)

Owners (proposed):
- LumenHealth: David Li (product lead), Sara Park (clinical QA)
- Redwood: Irene Choi (eng/sales lead), Marissa Cole (customer success), Karthik Iyer (ML infra lead)

Model shortlist (initial suggestion):
- Primary (open/hosted): Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized int4 for cost/latency) — good English/ES/PT baseline when instruction-tuned.
- Fallback (on-prem candidate): Llama-2-13B-q4 or ggml-llama2-13b-q4 — slightly larger but acceptable for offline failover.

Attachments: I attached a mutual action plan workbook with acceptance gates and a short model-profiles PDF. Please review and flag anything missing.

Ask: Can you confirm the owners above and sign off on the Week 0 deliverables (we can also convert the attached workbook into a shared checklist)?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Irene — notes below to include in the SOW and technical appendix. High-level recommendation and evaluation plan: 

Model recommendation:
- Primary (hosted): Mistral-Instruct-7B (instruction-tuned). Run quantized int4 for latency/cost. Baseline config: 1024 token context, top-p sampling with temperature 0.0 for deterministic classification/intent tasks.
- Fallback (on-prem air-gap): Llama-2-13B-q4 — to be used only for escalation workflow (requires separate infra).

Evaluation rubric (we'll produce a short script + notebook):
- Quality: intent macro F1 (>= 0.88 target) measured over 1k holdout samples; locale breakdown for EN/ES/PT.
- Safety/hallucination: run 200 curated edge-case prompts flagged by clinical QA; any unsafe output triggers remediation; acceptable manual false-positive rate <= 2%.
- Latency: p50 <= 250ms and p95 <= 700ms on Redwood hosted pool with minimal batching (we'll record token-level breakdown).
- Cost: estimated token cost and projected $/1k requests for current config; include delta for switching to quantized runtime or smaller model.

Data handling (paragraph you can paste into SOW):
"Redwood will ingest an anonymized test dataset provided by LumenHealth into a dedicated tenant. All stored artifacts will be encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (optional), request logs will be redact-configured to exclude PHI fields, and inference artifacts used for evaluation will be retained for up to 30 days unless otherwise specified. No production patient data will be stored beyond the agreed retention window."

Failover/runbook for fallback tests (high level):
1) Deploy trimmed Llama-2-13B-q4 on customer-supplied on-prem node or Redwood private VPC.
2) Simulate 5% of traffic to fall back pathway via routing policy for 2 hours, capture side-by-side comparisons.
3) Verify latency (p50/p95), correctness on 50 sampled messages, and circuit-breaker thresholds.

I'll attach a brief model-profile that maps expected latencies and cost estimates for the two model choices.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
ML Infra Lead | Redwood Inference
